Questions answered (of the nine): 4 (presence of a tagged animal near a receiver); 5 only if many tags are representative of the population
Questions not answered: 1; 2; 3; 6; 7; 8; 9; presence of untagged fish; absence between receivers
Data required: Coded transmitters in captured animals; moored receivers; receiver metadata; detection-range tests with sentinel tags (S11; S12; P301)
Spatial resolution: Receiver detection range (hundreds of metres typical; species- and condition-dependent; S11)
Temporal resolution: Seconds to minutes while the tag is in range; months until download unless cabled or modem-equipped
Positional uncertainty: Detection is presence-in-range not a point; range changes with noise depth and weather (S11)
Typical sample size: Study-dependent; usually tens to a few hundreds of tagged individuals per study (S02). Verified network example: Motus analogue lesson only (S03).
Representativeness issues: Tags describe tagged individuals. Capture location size sex and season bias the sample (S02; S118). Array geography is not the species range.
Handles detection gaps?: No. Silence is not absence (S11; P301).
Uncertainty output: Residency indices and detection histories; range tests if done; rarely a full posterior on location
Main assumptions: A detection means the tagged animal was within range; non-detection does not mean the animal left the study area unless range and coverage are known
Failure modes: Range collapse treated as emigration; overlapping arrays treated as one habitat; tag expulsion or battery death read as movement
Validation: Range tests; sentinel tags; comparison with active tracks where available (S11; P300)
Public-data feasibility: Low. Detections are usually embargoed; receiver maps can expose aggregations (S07; S08; S84; S85)
Relevance to FishAI: None on disk. Would answer Q4 internally after a partnership. Cannot feed a survey-detection product. FishAI has no telemetry.

Questions answered (of the nine): 4 (short-term activity centre of a tagged animal inside an overlapping array)
Questions not answered: 1; 2; 3; 5 as population movement; 6; 7; 8; 9; precise instantaneous location
Data required: Detections at multiple overlapping receivers plus planar receiver coordinates; analyst-chosen time window delta_t (P300)
Spatial resolution: Array scale; COA is a weighted mean of receiver locations not a GPS fix (P300)
Temporal resolution: Windows of 5 to 60 min were tested in the method paper (P300); window is a study choice
Positional uncertainty: A centre of activity not a point. Median distances between successive COAs were 28 to 42 percent of those from active tracking because of smoothing (P300).
Typical sample size: One COA series per tagged animal. Method paper used neonate blacktip sharks in a nursery array (P300).
Representativeness issues: Tags describe tagged individuals. Receiver geometry dominates the COA; animals outside overlapping coverage cannot be positioned (P300; P301).
Handles detection gaps?: No. Empty windows yield no COA. Gaps are not interpolated as true paths unless a later movement model is added.
Uncertainty output: Usually a point per window; not a calibrated error ellipse unless separately tested
Main assumptions: Overlapping detection ranges; detections in a window sample the activity centre; arithmetic mean of receiver positions weighted by detection frequency (P300)
Failure modes: Wrong delta_t; non-overlapping arrays; treating COAs as sequential GPS steps in a track model
Validation: Simulated tracks and active tracking in Simpfendorfer et al. 2002 (P300)
Public-data feasibility: Low. Requires raw detections and receiver coordinates from a partner array.
Relevance to FishAI: Requires telemetry FishAI does not have. Do not compute COAs from survey stations.

Questions answered (of the nine): 4 (fine-scale track of a tagged animal inside a time-of-arrival array)
Questions not answered: 1; 2; 3; 5 unless tags are representative; 6; 7; 8; 9
Data required: Synchronizing transmitters or synchronized clocks; three or more receivers; time-of-arrival or TDOA; speed of sound (P302; P304)
Spatial resolution: Metres inside a well-designed array
Temporal resolution: Each decoded ping that is heard by enough receivers
Positional uncertainty: Verified example: mean positional accuracy of a stationary transmitter 2.64 plus or minus 2.32 m; 2.13 plus or minus 1.31 m inside the array; 5.12 plus or minus 4.11 m outside (P302). Reservoir test: 3.3 m positioning error after HPE less than 15 filter (P303). HPE is unitless and not a calibrated metre error (P302 notes / manufacturer guidance).
Typical sample size: Multiple tagged animals simultaneously; Espinoza et al. used 16 VR2W receivers and 8 synchronizing transmitters (P302)
Representativeness issues: Tags describe tagged individuals. Positions exist only where geometry and detections allow. Outside-array positions are worse (P302; P303).
Handles detection gaps?: Partially for YAPS (random-walk process can bridge missing pings; P304) but large gaps widen process error. VPS does not invent positions from silence.
Uncertainty output: VPS: relative HPE not metres. YAPS: process and TOA error from the state-space fit (P304).
Main assumptions: Known hydrophone geometry; adequate clock sync; sound-speed model; animal inside or near the array
Failure modes: Clock drift; multipath; treating HPE as metres; reading tracks as the untagged population
Validation: Stationary and moving test transmitters; comparison with active tracking (P302); simulated known tracks for YAPS (P304)
Public-data feasibility: Very low. Proprietary VPS processing and/or raw TOA; not public for FishAI frames.
Relevance to FishAI: No array. Reef RVC cannot be treated as a VPS. Internal research only if a partner supplies data.

Questions answered (of the nine): 4 at network nodes; 5 only as coarse passage between arrays if tagging is representative
Questions not answered: 1; 2; 3; 6; 7; 8; 9; continuous tracks between arrays
Data required: Shared tag protocol; station metadata; data-sharing agreements (OTN S07; ATN S08). Inspired Motus on land (S03).
Spatial resolution: Station range only (S03; S11)
Temporal resolution: Continuous while in range; delayed by download and embargo
Positional uncertainty: Station-level presence
Typical sample size: Network-scale: many projects. OTN launched 2010 with CFI infrastructure funding of 35 million CAD plus NSERC 10 million CAD (S07; verified in Iverson et al. 2019). Animal counts are project-specific and not a census.
Representativeness issues: Arrays sit where researchers can moor them. Tagged animals come from capture sites. Cross-project detections still describe tagged individuals (S02; S07).
Handles detection gaps?: No. Coverage holes are not absence.
Uncertainty output: Detection histories; embargo flags; range tests if contributed
Main assumptions: Compatible frequencies and ID codes; metadata sufficient to interpret a detection
Failure modes: False positives after filtering increase false negatives (Motus lesson; S03); sensitive-species rules block reuse (S84; S85)
Validation: Array metadata and range tests (S11); data-policy compliance (S08)
Public-data feasibility: Partnership and delayed access. ATN DAC is a community aggregator with owner-controlled release (S08; P322).
Relevance to FishAI: The marine analogue of Motus. High for a future internal movement layer. Zero public detections in the repo.

Questions answered (of the nine): 4 for tagged animals that surface or fly
Questions not answered: 1; 2; 3; 6; 7; 8; 9; fully aquatic reef-fish tracks; population distribution unless tagging is representative
Data required: Platform transmitter terminals; Argos locations with location class or Kalman error ellipses; surfacing (S13; S02)
Spatial resolution: Hundreds of metres to tens of kilometres depending on location class
Temporal resolution: Several fixes per day when at the surface
Positional uncertainty: Verified 68th percentile errors versus Fastloc GPS: LC-3 0.49 km; LC-2 1.01 km; LC-1 1.20 km; LC-0 4.18 km; LC-A 6.19 km; LC-B 10.28 km (S13; Costa et al. 2010). Errors were right-skewed and larger than vendor declarations.
Typical sample size: Costa et al. compared 7318 Argos and 27046 GPS positions from 27 pinnipeds of five species; 1105 Argos-GPS pairs within five minutes (S13).
Representativeness issues: Tags describe tagged individuals. Animals that rarely surface yield few or poor fixes. Capture and handling bias (S02; S118).
Handles detection gaps?: No; gaps when submerged. State-space filters (aniMotum) can interpolate with widening uncertainty (P305; S53).
Uncertainty output: Location class or error ellipse; filtered posterior locations if an SSM is fitted
Main assumptions: Transmitter reached the satellite; error model matches the location class or ellipse
Failure modes: Using LC-B as a precise point; applying Argos to animals that do not surface; treating a few sharks as the stock
Validation: Double-tag Fastloc GPS (S13); holdout locations after SSM (P305)
Public-data feasibility: Some Movebank and ATN datasets; many embargoed (S04; S08)
Relevance to FishAI: Not usable for Keys/PR/USVI/FGB/SBC reef fishes that do not surface. Pelagic partners only.

Questions answered (of the nine): 4 at surfacing for tagged air-breathers or briefly surfacing animals
Questions not answered: 1 through 3; 5 through 9; any fully aquatic fish that never surfaces
Data required: Fastloc GPS snapshot during a brief surface interval plus satellite relay (S13; S19)
Spatial resolution: Tens of metres when a fix is obtained
Temporal resolution: Each successful surfacing
Positional uncertainty: On-land stationary Fastloc GPS 36 m versus handheld GPS about 3 m; still about four times better than Argos LC-3 at 150 m in that test (S13)
Typical sample size: Same 27 pinnipeds as the Argos comparison (S13). Typical wildlife studies remain small samples of catchable animals.
Representativeness issues: Tags describe tagged individuals. GPS does not work underwater (S19).
Handles detection gaps?: No underwater.
Uncertainty output: Per-fix GPS quality; missed-fix rates
Main assumptions: Sky view at the surface; tag mass acceptable (S17)
Failure modes: Claiming reef-fish tracks; missed fixes under poor sky view
Validation: Stationary tests and dual Argos-Fastloc tags (S13)
Public-data feasibility: Some Movebank datasets; not for FishAI survey species
Relevance to FishAI: Does not work for fully aquatic reef and kelp fishes. Do not use.

Questions answered (of the nine): 4 (coarse reconstructed path of a tagged pelagic animal); depth-temperature habitat of that animal
Questions not answered: 1; 2; 3; 6; 7; 8; 9; reef-scale location; untagged fish
Data required: Pop-up satellite archival tag; light and/or SST series; satellite SST fields for latitude; known-release or pop-up endpoint (S14; P307)
Spatial resolution: Tens to hundreds of kilometres for reconstructed daily positions
Temporal resolution: Daily geolocation; depth and temperature every few minutes; data after pop-up or recovery
Positional uncertainty: Verified RMSE: light-level longitude 0.89 deg and 0.55 deg for salmon sharks and blue sharks; SST latitude 1.47 deg and 1.16 deg. Atlantic bluefin archival: longitude 0.78 deg latitude 0.90 deg; transmitted PSAT: 1.30 deg and 1.89 deg (P307). Equinox latitude collapse remains a light-geolocation failure mode (S15).
Typical sample size: Musyl et al. analysed 731 author deployments on 19 species and 1433 deployments on 24 species from 53 papers (S14). Reporting rate 0.79 (95 percent CI 0.76 to 0.82) authors versus 0.76 (0.74 to 0.78) literature. Retention median 53 days versus programmed median 242 days (S14).
Representativeness issues: Tags describe tagged individuals. Premature release and non-reporting bias surviving tracks (S14). Capture location bias (S09).
Handles detection gaps?: Process models interpolate between daily geolocations with large error; they do not recover true paths through equinoxes (S15; S53).
Uncertainty output: Geolocation RMSE if double-tagged; SSM posteriors if fitted; otherwise often unstated
Main assumptions: Light or SST uniquely identifies longitude/latitude; tag SST matches satellite SST (P307 simulations: SST mismatch dominates latitude error)
Failure modes: Premature pop-off; treating a 100 km error path as a reef map; reading particles or survey pins as PSAT tracks
Validation: Double-tag Argos or GPS endpoints (P307); recapture GPS (P307)
Public-data feasibility: Some published tracks; raw archives often restricted
Relevance to FishAI: Not a reef nowcast input. Irrelevant to RVC and SBC frames.

Questions answered (of the nine): 4 for tagged demersal fish that rest on the seabed for a tidal cycle on a shelf with a unique tide
Questions not answered: 1; 2; 3; 6; 7; 8; 9; mid-water swimming periods; coral-reef or kelp-forest frames without a usable tidal fingerprint
Data required: Depth-archival tags; tidal database from a numerical model; periods of seabed rest (P308; P309)
Spatial resolution: Tens of kilometres; tidal-model grid 12 km in the North Sea application (P309)
Temporal resolution: When the fish rests for one or more tidal cycles; not while swimming in mid-water (P309)
Positional uncertainty: Predicted often within 40 km sometimes 10 km; moored-tag checks 15.7 plus or minus 3.5 km of true location; free fish within 5 days of release 35 plus or minus 24 km of release and 37 plus or minus 23 km of recapture (P308)
Typical sample size: 752 mature female plaice tagged 1993 to 1999; 20403 days from 145 fish (P309). Not a population census.
Representativeness issues: Tags describe tagged individuals. Method needs a shelf with spatially unique tides. Recapture-dependent archives bias toward fished areas.
Handles detection gaps?: No location while the fish is off the bottom (P309).
Uncertainty output: Cluster spread of matching tidal cells; sometimes reduced with depth and SST filters (P309)
Main assumptions: Fish on seabed for a full tide; tidal model skill; unique (high-water time range) pairs
Failure modes: Ambiguous distant matches; applying the method where tides are not unique (Keys/PR reefs); treating locations as GPS
Validation: Moored tags; near-release and near-recapture comparisons (P308)
Public-data feasibility: Historical CEFAS-style datasets exist in papers; not in FishAI; not applicable to current frames
Relevance to FishAI: Not applicable to RVC reef cylinders or SBC kelp transects.

Questions answered (of the nine): 4 (filtered locations and move-persistence of a tagged animal from noisy Argos or similar fixes)
Questions not answered: 1; 2; 3; 6; 7; 8; 9; untagged animals; survey detection
Data required: Ordered individual fixes with an error model (Argos LS classes or KF ellipses; optionally GPS or light geolocation used with caution) (P305; S52; S53)
Spatial resolution: That of the filtered track; still individual-scale
Temporal resolution: Fitted at observation times plus user-chosen regular prediction steps (P305)
Positional uncertainty: Process plus observation error; widening across gaps (S52; S54)
Typical sample size: One SSM per individual; packages batch many animals. Sample is still the tagged set.
Representativeness issues: Tags describe tagged individuals. Quality-controlled tracks are not a density surface (S02).
Handles detection gaps?: Partially: predicts through gaps with increasing uncertainty; long gaps are not true observations (P305; S54).
Uncertainty output: Location variance; move-persistence time series (P305)
Main assumptions: Continuous-time movement process; correctly specified observation error; animals not reflecting off unmodelled barriers unless added
Failure modes: Fitting an SSM to unordered survey pins; treating predicted locations as GPS; population maps from a few tracks
Validation: Holdout locations; simulation; comparison with GPS on the same animal (S53; P305)
Public-data feasibility: Software is public; tracks usually are not
Relevance to FishAI: No tracks to filter. Do not run aniMotum on RVC stations.

Questions answered (of the nine): 4 (behavioral states along a tagged track; e.g. resident vs traveling)
Questions not answered: 1; 2; 3; 6; 7; 8; 9; ecological labels unless independently validated
Data required: Regular or regularized ordered tracks or sensor series (S55; S56)
Spatial resolution: That of the track
Temporal resolution: Step interval of the series; HSMM adds dwell-time distributions (S55)
Positional uncertainty: State-assignment probabilities; not a new location technology
Typical sample size: Per individual; pooling individuals needs random effects. Short tracks overfit (S55).
Representativeness issues: Tags describe tagged individuals. States are statistical not named behaviours unless video-validated.
Handles detection gaps?: Poorly. Irregular gaps violate discrete-time HMM assumptions unless preprocessed (S54 is the continuous-time alternative).
Uncertainty output: Viterbi path plus state probabilities; pseudo-residuals (S55; S56)
Main assumptions: Markov or semi-Markov state switching; emission distributions match the data
Failure modes: Biological labels glued onto unnamed states; HMM on occurrence points rather than tracks (forbidden in methods/MOVEMENT_MODEL_MATRIX.csv)
Validation: Pseudo-residuals; holdout; labelled behaviour where available (S55)
Public-data feasibility: Software public (momentuHMM; S56); data restricted
Relevance to FishAI: No tracks. Not a detection model for RVC.

Questions answered (of the nine): 4 (continuous-time correlated random walk path of a tagged animal with irregular fixes)
Questions not answered: 1; 2; 3; 5 as population; 6; 7; 8; 9
Data required: Irregular ordered locations with times (S54)
Spatial resolution: Individual path
Temporal resolution: Continuous-time; handles irregular sampling (S54)
Positional uncertainty: Process and measurement variance; long gaps widen uncertainty (S54)
Typical sample size: Per tagged animal
Representativeness issues: Tags describe tagged individuals.
Handles detection gaps?: Partially via the continuous-time process; gaps are not observations.
Uncertainty output: Predicted location covariance
Main assumptions: Velocity autocorrelation; Gaussian errors unless extended
Failure modes: Survey stations as successive steps; barrier-unaware paths across land or reef
Validation: Holdout locations (S54)
Public-data feasibility: Software public; tracks restricted
Relevance to FishAI: No irregular telemetry series exist in the repo.

Questions answered (of the nine): 4 (space used between consecutive fixes of a tagged animal)
Questions not answered: 1; 2; 3; 6; 7; 8; 9; home range if sampling is too short (S59; S60; S106)
Data required: Ordered locations with times (S59; S60)
Spatial resolution: Bridge between consecutive fixes; sensitive to fix interval
Temporal resolution: Between-fix intervals; dBBMM uses a moving window on variance (S60)
Positional uncertainty: Brownian-bridge variance; dBBMM allows time-varying Brownian motion variance (S60)
Typical sample size: Per individual
Representativeness issues: Tags describe tagged individuals. Bridges are not population density.
Handles detection gaps?: The bridge fills the gap by assumption of Brownian motion; large gaps produce unrealistically wide or wrong corridors (S59).
Uncertainty output: Utilization raster with bridge variance; not always a confidence interval on area
Main assumptions: Conditional Brownian motion between known endpoints; dBBMM relaxes constant variance (S60)
Failure modes: Constant-variance BBMM on mixed rest/travel; using the bridge as a known path
Validation: Holdout locations (S59; S60)
Public-data feasibility: Software public; tracks restricted
Relevance to FishAI: No tracks. Not for survey pins.

Questions answered (of the nine): 4 (home-range or occurrence distribution of a tagged animal)
Questions not answered: 1 as population density; 2; 3; 6; 7; 8; 9
Data required: Ordered tracks; ctmm workflow uses a fitted continuous-time model before AKDE (P306; S106)
Spatial resolution: Individual range; bandwidth set by the movement model for AKDE
Temporal resolution: Requires enough duration for a home range to exist; not a daily nowcast
Positional uncertainty: AKDE accounts for autocorrelation; conventional IID KDE underestimates range on autocorrelated GPS (S106). Empirical: AKDE 95 percent areas larger than IID KDE by a mean factor of 2 across 369 individuals of 27 species; conventional estimates were negatively biased as effective sample size fell (P323).
Typical sample size: Per individual. Noonan et al. used 369 individuals 27 species five continents (P323).
Representativeness issues: Tags describe tagged individuals. A home range is not a stock map.
Handles detection gaps?: AKDE uses the autocorrelation model; it does not invent unsampled habitats the animal never used.
Uncertainty output: Confidence intervals on home-range area; effective sample size N_area (S106; P323)
Main assumptions: Range residency for a home-range estimator; occurrence distributions answer a different question (P306)
Failure modes: IID KDE on high-frequency tracks; reporting a range from too few independent crossings of the range (S106)
Validation: Half-sample cross-validation of coverage (P323); simulation (S106)
Public-data feasibility: ctmm is public; tracks usually not
Relevance to FishAI: No tracks. Do not kernel-smooth RVC detections as home ranges.

Questions answered (of the nine): 4 (probability of a tagged animal occurring in space given the observed track)
Questions not answered: 1; 2; 3; 6; 7; 8; 9; probability that an untagged fish is there
Data required: A UD estimator (KDE AKDE BBMM or equivalent) plus the track (S59; S106; P301)
Spatial resolution: Individual space-use raster
Temporal resolution: The period of the track not the survey calendar
Positional uncertainty: Inherited from the estimator (S106; P323)
Typical sample size: Per tagged animal
Representativeness issues: Tags describe tagged individuals. Pooling UDs without a design is not a population UD.
Handles detection gaps?: Depends on the estimator; see KDE/akde and BBMM rows.
Uncertainty output: UD height is not automatically a calibrated probability of population occurrence
Main assumptions: The track is a sample from the animal's use process during that period
Failure modes: Publishing a UD as a fishing map (S84); averaging a few UDs as Q1
Validation: Same as the underlying estimator
Public-data feasibility: Low for marine fish; coarsen or withhold (S84; S85)
Relevance to FishAI: Internal only after telemetry. Never a public globe layer.

Questions answered (of the nine): 4 (habitat selection along observed steps of tagged animals); simulated space use under habitat if the movement model is then projected
Questions not answered: 1 as occurrence probability without a survey likelihood; 2; 3; 6; 7; 8; 9
Data required: Ordered used steps plus available steps; habitat covariates at both (S57; S58)
Spatial resolution: Step length scale of the telemetry
Temporal resolution: Step interval
Positional uncertainty: Selection coefficients with standard errors; availability definition dominates inference (S57)
Typical sample size: Multiple individuals recommended; cross-validate by individual (S57; S58)
Representativeness issues: Tags describe tagged individuals. Availability radius is an analyst choice (S57).
Handles detection gaps?: No. Steps cannot be built across large gaps without an SSM first.
Uncertainty output: Coefficient intervals; iSSA jointly estimates movement and selection (S58)
Main assumptions: Used and available steps are correctly defined; habitat layers match the animal's grain
Failure modes: SSF on unordered survey presence; treating relative selection as Q2 detection probability
Validation: Leave-one-individual-out (S57; S58)
Public-data feasibility: Needs tracks plus habitat rasters FishAI does not have (habitat folder empty)
Relevance to FishAI: Requires telemetry. Habitat joins are for survey models first not SSF.

Questions answered (of the nine): 4 (whether tagged individuals return to or remain in a site); 5 only if the tagged sample is representative
Data required: Repeat detections at known stations or recaptures; residency indices (P301)
Spatial resolution: Site or array
Temporal resolution: Days to years depending on battery and study
Positional uncertainty: Site-level not a track
Typical sample size: Tagged subset at that site
Representativeness issues: Tags describe tagged individuals. High site fidelity in tagged fish does not mean the survey frame is closed.
Handles detection gaps?: No. Non-detection is not confirmed emigration (S11; P301).
Uncertainty output: Residency index distributions; sometimes survival/emigration if a mark-recapture model is added
Main assumptions: Detection probability modelled or range-tested; site definition matches ecology
Failure modes: Equating array residency with stock structure; using fidelity to skip detection models on RVC
Validation: Range tests; comparison of indices (P301)
Public-data feasibility: Partner arrays; not public in FishAI
Relevance to FishAI: Could later explain why some RVC species are easier to detect at the same sites but cannot be estimated now.

Questions answered (of the nine): 5 (movement rates between spatial strata from recoveries if tagging and recapture cover those strata); two-point movement not a continuous track
Questions not answered: 4 as a path; 1; 2; 6; 7; 8; 9; daily location
Data required: Releases by stratum; recoveries with reporting model; catch or effort in each stratum (P310)
Spatial resolution: Strata of the tagging design not metres
Temporal resolution: Release-to-recovery interval; often months to years
Positional uncertainty: Two points only; path unknown (S113 analogue for birds)
Typical sample size: Can be large in tuna programs; still not a census. Reporting is effort-biased (P310; S113).
Representativeness issues: Recoveries concentrate where people fish or search (S113). Hilborn 1990: reliable movement rates need tagging and recapture in each stratum (P310).
Handles detection gaps?: No path between points.
Uncertainty output: Likelihood intervals on movement rates if the observation model is specified (P310)
Main assumptions: Reporting probabilities; tag loss and tagging mortality if included (P310)
Failure modes: Straight lines between release and recapture; ignoring reporting bias
Validation: Diagnostics on residuals; coverage of strata (P310)
Public-data feasibility: Some historical recovery files; fishery-dependent; partnership
Relevance to FishAI: No conventional-tag database. Not a substitute for RVC detection models.

Questions answered (of the nine): 6 (parentage: realized larval dispersal between sampled adults and juveniles); CKMR estimates adult abundance and survival not maps (S47; S48)
Questions not answered: 4 adult tracks; 1 as a live map; 2; 7; 8; 9; CKMR is not a location method
Data required: Intensive tissue sampling of adults and juveniles; genotypes; for CKMR also ages and a kinship model (S47; P311; P312)
Spatial resolution: Among sampled reefs or populations; Almany et al. 2017 spanned about 10000 km2 and eight sites (P311)
Temporal resolution: The larval cohort sampled (years of field work) not a daily forecast
Positional uncertainty: Assignment error of parentage methods; incomplete adult sampling misses parents (P311)
Typical sample size: Verified: clownfish mean observed dispersal 15 km in 2009 and 10 km in 2011; Laplacian kernel mean 13 to 19 km with 90 percent of settlement within 31 to 43 km; butterflyfish mean 43 to 64 km (P311). CKMR example: 214 juvenile white sharks; adult estimate later revised to about 750 (470 to 1030) (S48).
Representativeness issues: Assignments are among sampled fish. Unsampled spawning sites are invisible. CKMR abundance is not a location (S48).
Handles detection gaps?: Not a detection-gap method. Unsampled adults are missing parents.
Uncertainty output: Dispersal kernels with model-selection; CKMR confidence intervals (S47; S48; P311)
Main assumptions: Parentage power; closed or modelled unsampled adults; CKMR kinship and stock structure (S47)
Failure modes: A few parent-offspring pairs treated as the connectivity matrix; CKMR sold as a map
Validation: Simulation of assignment; multi-year replication (P311); CKMR simulation (S47)
Public-data feasibility: Genotypes are typically restricted; papers report summaries
Relevance to FishAI: Needed to validate any larval particle product (P312). FishAI has no tissue archive. One CalCOFI egg cruise is not parentage.

Questions answered (of the nine): 6 (natal origin or environmental history of an individual fish); sometimes 5 as reconstructed movement among chemically distinct waters
Questions not answered: 2; 4 as a GPS track; 7; 8; 9; adult occurrence maps
Data required: Otoliths with chronology; water chemistry baselines; assays (P313)
Spatial resolution: Chemically distinct water masses not metres
Temporal resolution: Daily to annual increments depending on assay (P313)
Positional uncertainty: Classification error among source groups; physiology filters chemistry so environment is not a 1:1 map (P313)
Typical sample size: Tens to hundreds of otoliths per study; not verified here as a single global n
Representativeness issues: Sacrificed or archived fish; baselines must cover true sources. Campana 1999: not all applications are firmly based because of physiological filters (P313).
Handles detection gaps?: Not a gap-filling location method.
Uncertainty output: Classification probabilities if a mixing model is used
Main assumptions: Otoliths are metabolically inert recorders; source signatures differ and are stable (P313)
Failure modes: Assigning natal reefs from overlapping chemistries; using otoliths as live locations
Validation: Known-origin marks; water-otolith calibration (P313)
Public-data feasibility: Laboratory data; partnership
Relevance to FishAI: A validation stream for Q6 not a product. No otolith library in the repo.

Questions answered (of the nine): 6 (connectivity probabilities under stated current fields and larval rules). Particles are not adult movement.
Questions not answered: 1 adult distribution; 2 survey detection; 4 adult tracks; 5 adult seasonal redistribution; 7; 8 unless currents are archived forecasts and skill is shown; 9 as adult climate range
Data required: Ocean velocity at larval depths; spawning times and places; pelagic larval duration; mortality and vertical behaviour if claimed (S62; S63; P314; P315)
Spatial resolution: That of the hydrodynamic grid not a finer biological truth
Temporal resolution: Simulation time step; spawning season of the scenario
Positional uncertainty: Current error plus behaviour assumptions (S62). OpenDrift notes operational oil/SAR use; biological modules are user-specified (P314).
Typical sample size: Thousands to millions of particles per scenario (OpenDrift: millions on a laptop claimed by authors; P314). Particles are not fish.
Representativeness issues: Release sites and traits are assumptions. Passive particles are not fish behaviour (S62; P312). FishAI has one CalCOFI cruise 202204 and HYCOM; spawning maps are missing and sensitive.
Handles detection gaps?: Not applicable. This is a forward simulation not a gap-fill of observations.
Uncertainty output: Ensemble of particles if run; often omitted. Should be connectivity probabilities not tracks (S63).
Main assumptions: Hydrodynamics adequate at larval depth; biological modules correct. Incorrect behaviour can be worse than passive (P312).
Failure modes: Reading particle paths as adult movement; unvalidated CMS/OpenDrift/Ichthyop as a nowcast; publishing spawning sites
Validation: Must be separate (parentage otoliths recruitment); see next row
Public-data feasibility: Software public (S63; P314; P315). Skill is not public until validation data exist.
Relevance to FishAI: Q6 only after biology parameters and a validation partnership. Eggs are not adults (S119). Do not fit HMM/SSM to particles.

Questions answered (of the nine): 6 (whether a biophysical connectivity model matches independent biological data)
Questions not answered: 4 adult movement; 2; 7; 8; any claim without a held-out biological dataset
Data required: Parentage or otolith or recruitment time series that the model did not use (P312; S62)
Spatial resolution: That of the parentage or otolith design
Temporal resolution: The years of genetic or recruitment sampling
Positional uncertainty: Statistical goodness-of-fit not a metre error. Bode et al. 2019 used maximum likelihood and parametric bootstrap GoF on Plectropomus maculatus parentage in the southern Great Barrier Reef (P312).
Typical sample size: Set by the parentage study not by particle count (P312)
Representativeness issues: Parentage is spatially and temporally limited; a pass in one seascape is not a global larval model (P312).
Handles detection gaps?: Tests models; does not fill adult survey gaps.
Uncertainty output: Model weights; exclusion of poor models. Parentage can reject bad biophysical models (P312).
Main assumptions: Independence of validation data; sampling design of parentage captured the relevant links
Failure modes: Tuning behaviour to the same parentage used as the test; claiming adult nowcasts from a larval pass
Validation: This row is the validation. Bode et al.: species-specific behaviour beat passive; wrong behaviour was worse than ignoring behaviour (P312).
Public-data feasibility: Parentage datasets rarely fully public
Relevance to FishAI: Blocking gap. No genetic or recruitment validation set. Do not publish connectivity.

Questions answered (of the nine): 5 (interannual shift of the abundance-weighted centre within the survey domain); 1 and 3 as model-based density/index if the survey supports them
Questions not answered: 4 individual routes; 6; 7; 8; seasonal movement if the survey is one season; COG outside the survey frame
Data required: Repeated surveys with locations zeros and effort; spatiotemporal GLMM (S72; S73; P316)
Spatial resolution: Extrapolation grid of the model; Keys RVC 200 m cells in the design paper (S41) but COG is a domain summary
Temporal resolution: Survey year or season. RVC is biennial in summer; SBC is annual late July-August at 11 sites.
Positional uncertainty: Model-based COG has standard errors; sample-weighted averages confound effort shifts (P316).
Typical sample size: Verified case: two U.S. West Coast datasets 1977 to 2013 for 18 fishes; SDF COG showed significant northward shifts for 6 of 18 and southward for 2 (P316).
Representativeness issues: COG is inside the sampled domain. Eleven SBC sites cannot support a regional COG. Summer-only RVC cannot show winter redistribution.
Handles detection gaps?: Spatial random fields interpolate unsampled cells inside the domain; that is not a nowcast and can invent biomass off the frame (S72).
Uncertainty output: SE and CI on eastings/northings of COG (P316; S73 get_index)
Main assumptions: Catchability constant within the program; spatial coverage adequate; zeros are real survey zeros
Failure modes: AWA COG when the survey footprint moves (P316); COG on 11 kelp sites; treating COG as Q4
Validation: Simulation vs AWA (P316); untouched later years (S72; S73)
Public-data feasibility: Keys RVC zeros exist (S120) after habitat joins. Trawl series in the repo are incomplete.
Relevance to FishAI: Defensible interannual COG only on Keys-scale stratified RVC after spatial modelling. Not seasonal. Not SBC-11.

Questions answered (of the nine): 5 (change in distribution between seasons when the same protocol samples those seasons)
Questions not answered: 4 daily movement; 6; 7; 8; anything from a single-season series
Data required: Repeated standardized surveys across seasons (S111; S72) or representative tags
Spatial resolution: Survey domain
Temporal resolution: Season
Positional uncertainty: That of the survey index or occupancy estimator
Typical sample size: Full seasonal trawl programs; not FishAI's current holdings (one DATRAS quarter; S104)
Representativeness issues: Protocol change between seasons is not ecology (S111). RVC and SBC are warm-season only.
Handles detection gaps?: No. Missing seasons are missing.
Uncertainty output: Seasonal fields or occupancy colonization/extinction if repeats exist (S111)
Main assumptions: Comparable catchability across seasons or an explicit catchability model
Failure modes: Inferring winter kelp-bass distribution from July-August transects; treating biennial RVC as seasonal
Validation: Later seasons and years; tag-survey agreement if tags exist (CORE_PROBLEM_DEFINITION)
Public-data feasibility: Needs a multi-season trawl or visual program. Not present.
Relevance to FishAI: Cannot be done with current frames. Kelp bass 2022 failure is a year effect not a season effect.

Questions answered (of the nine): 4 (vertical movement of tagged or insonified animals); observation-process covariate for 2 and 3 (availability to a survey)
Questions not answered: 1 horizontal distribution; 6; 7; 8; 9
Data required: Depth series from tags or calibrated echosounders plus species identification from trawls or video (P317; S34)
Spatial resolution: Water-column at the tag or along the acoustic transect
Temporal resolution: Diel (24 h) (P317)
Positional uncertainty: Depth of the tag or backscatter layer; species identity from acoustics alone is not resolved (S34)
Typical sample size: Tagged subset or survey transects. Not in FishAI.
Representativeness issues: DVM can be facultative not obligate and changes with ontogeny and environment (P317). Acoustic layers are mixed species without ground truth (S34).
Handles detection gaps?: Acoustics miss fish in the surface blind zone and near the bottom; tags miss untagged fish.
Uncertainty output: Depth distributions by hour; target-strength error if biomass is attempted
Main assumptions: The observed depth cycle is ecological not only gear avoidance; species apportionment if biomass is claimed
Failure modes: A night-time acoustic layer read as a single reef species; ignoring DVM in a daytime-only diver survey's detectability
Validation: Tag depth vs echosounder; trawl composition (S34; P317)
Public-data feasibility: No echosounder or depth-tag series in the repo
Relevance to FishAI: Possible later as an observation covariate. RVC is daytime divers. Not a location product.

Questions answered (of the nine): 1 and 4 jointly when telemetry and survey/distribution data share parameters (P318; S69)
Questions not answered: 2 unless the survey likelihood is explicit; 6; 7; 8 without archived environment; untagged real-time location
Data required: Individual tracks plus a population observation stream (surveys or effort-standardized checklists) with a formal link (P318; S69; S70)
Spatial resolution: That of the scaled-up movement process plus the survey grid
Temporal resolution: That of both data types; eBird examples are weekly (S79) not FishAI's biennial dives
Positional uncertainty: Joint posterior; telemetry error plus survey detection
Typical sample size: Needs enough tagged animals to represent movement types plus a designed survey. Published IMMs are terrestrial birds not reef fish (P318).
Representativeness issues: If tags are unrepresentative the joint model imports that bias into the distribution (S02; P318).
Handles detection gaps?: Movement model can spread mass between surveys; that is an assumption not an observation.
Uncertainty output: Shared-parameter posteriors if Bayesian; otherwise easy to understate
Main assumptions: The individual movement model scales to the population; observation models remain separate (S69)
Failure modes: Sticking an HMM onto RVC; claiming a nowcast; public tracks
Validation: Withheld tracks and withheld surveys separately (P318)
Public-data feasibility: No telemetry. Surveys exist. Integration is blocked.
Relevance to FishAI: A research direction after a telemetry partnership and a working survey-detection model. Not now.
